title: Quantum Transformations
description:
We want to be able to transform one quantum state to another quantum state. Quantum **gates** are valid quantum state transformations that are given by unitary operations. 


Look at the probabilities, amplitudes, and histogram on the right. We start with each qubit (quantum bit) in the ground state $\ket0$ with 100% probability. 
Drag and drop the $X$ gate to flip this to $\ket1$!
explanation: $X$ gate is the quantum equivalent of the NOT gate for classical computers with respect to the standard basis $\ket0, \ket1$. It flips $\ket0$ to $\ket1$, and $\ket1$ to $\ket0$.

title: X gate
description:
The $X$ gate you just saw transforms $$\ket 0$$ into $$\ket 1$$, and $$\ket 1$$ into $$\ket 0$$. It is thus the quantum equivalent of the NOT gate for classical computers.
 
It is represented as $$X = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix} = \ket0\bra1 + \ket1\bra0$$


In this circuit, the state after the hidden elements is $\ket{01}$ as seen in the results panel. Drag and drop the correct gates to transform the circuit to $\ket{10}$
explanation: Note that the $X$ gate are *involutory*, which means that applying them twice effectively does nothing! You'll notice this later in many of our other gates as well.
